question: Who was the temporary president of the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held on December 09, 1946? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: VT Krishnamachari
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Harendra Kumar Mukherjee
Sachchidanand Sinha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sachchidanand Sinha

Explanation:
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946. Being the eldest member, Sachchidanand Sinha was elected as the temporary president to preside over the meeting. He served until Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president on 11 December 1946. Sachchidanand Sinha was a senior leader from Bihar and a member of the Indian National Congress. His role as interim chairman was crucial in the initial proceedings of the Assembly.

question: The Indian citizen who is normally living outside India and have an Indian passport, (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Overseas Citizenship of India
Non-Resident Indians
Multi-Country Citizens
‎Inner Line Permit Citizens
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-Resident Indians

Explanation:
An Indian citizen who lives outside India and holds an Indian passport is called a Non-Resident Indian (NRI). NRI status applies to those who are ordinarily residing abroad for employment, business, or other purposes. Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) is for foreign nationals of Indian origin, not Indian citizens. 'Multi-Country Citizens' is not an official term. 'Inner Line Permit' is a document required for entry into certain northeastern states. NRIs have voting rights and can invest in India under specific schemes.

☛ Full form of OCI → Overseas Citizenship of India
☛ PIO card → Merged with OCI now

☛ Indian passport holder → Only NRI, not OCI

question: The provision of 'amendment in Indian constitution' was taken from which country's constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Weimar Constitution of Germany
Constitution of South Africa
American Constitution
Constitution of the USSR
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitution of South Africa

Explanation:
India's constitutional amendment process is borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa. The amendment procedure in Article 368 (Part XX) requires a special majority in Parliament and, in some cases, ratification by states. This model of flexible yet rigid amendment was inspired by South Africa's constitution. In contrast, the Weimar Constitution of Germany influenced emergency provisions, the American Constitution provided fundamental rights, and the USSR Constitution contributed fundamental duties. The borrowing of the amendment provision reflects India's adaptability in framing its supreme law.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ From which constitution is India's amendment procedure taken? → South Africa
☛ Which article deals with constitutional amendment? → Article 368
☛ Which part of Indian Constitution covers amendments? → Part XX
☛ What other feature is borrowed from South Africa? → Election of Rajya Sabha members
☛ Which provision is taken from Weimar Constitution? → Emergency powers
question_hi: 'भारतीय संविधान में संशोधन' का प्रावधान किस देश के संविधान से लिया गया था? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: जर्मनी का वाइमर संविधान
दक्षिण अफ्रीका का संविधान
अमेरिकी संविधान
सोवियत संघ का संविधान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दक्षिण अफ्रीका का संविधान

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में संशोधन प्रक्रिया दक्षिण अफ्रीका के संविधान से ली गई है। संवैधानिक संशोधन के लिए भारत में विशेष बहुमत की आवश्यकता होती है, जो दक्षिण अफ्रीकी मॉडल पर आधारित है। भारतीय संविधान के भाग XX (अनुच्छेद 368) में संशोधन की प्रक्रिया का उल्लेख है। यह प्रक्रिया संसद के दोनों सदनों में विशेष बहुमत और कुछ मामलों में राज्यों की सहमति की मांग करती है। अन्य विकल्प: वाइमर संविधान से आपातकालीन प्रावधान, अमेरिकी संविधान से मौलिक अधिकार, और सोवियत संघ से मौलिक कर्तव्य लिए गए।

question: The principle of Directive Principle of State Policy was taken from which the constitution of which country? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: American Constitution
UK Constitution
Constitution of Ireland
Constitution of the USSR
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitution of Ireland

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution (Part IV, Articles 36-51) were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. The Irish Constitution of 1937 incorporated principles of social and economic justice. The Indian Constituent Assembly adopted these principles to guide the state in policy-making. These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they are fundamental in governance. Other options: Fundamental Rights from the USA, Parliamentary system from the UK, and Socialist ideology from the USSR.

question: Who is the highest law officer of the state? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Law and Justice Minister
Advocate General
Chief Justice of India
Attorney General of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Advocate General

Explanation:
The highest law officer of the state is the Advocate General, appointed by the Governor under Article 165 of the Constitution. The Advocate General provides legal advice to the state government and represents the state in courts. This position is analogous to the Attorney General of India at the state level. The Law and Justice Minister is a political post, while the Advocate General is a constitutional office. The Chief Justice of India and the Attorney General of India are national-level positions, not state-level. Therefore, the correct option is Advocate General.

Solution: सही उत्तर है महाधिवक्ता

Explanation:
राज्य का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी महाधिवक्ता (Advocate General) होता है, जिसकी नियुक्ति राज्यपाल द्वारा की जाती है। यह पद अनुच्छेद 165 के तहत प्रावधानित है। महाधिवक्ता राज्य सरकार को कानूनी सलाह देता है और राज्य के मामलों में न्यायालय में प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। वह भारत के महान्यायवादी के समान राज्य स्तर पर भूमिका निभाता है। विधि एवं न्याय मंत्री एक राजनीतिक पद है, जबकि महाधिवक्ता एक संवैधानिक पद है। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश और भारत के महान्यायवादी राष्ट्रीय स्तर के पद हैं, राज्य स्तर के नहीं। इसलिए सही विकल्प महाधिवक्ता है।

question: "No person can be punished more than one for the same crime." What is this principle called? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Double Jeopardy
Single Penalty
Self Estrangement
Multiple Penalties
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Double Jeopardy

Explanation:
This principle states that no person can be punished more than once for the same crime. It is called the principle of Double Jeopardy. It is a fundamental right provided under Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution. According to this, if a person has already been convicted or punished for an offence, they cannot be prosecuted again for the same offence. This principle protects an individual from arbitrary actions of the state and ensures fairness in the judicial process. In the United States Constitution, this principle is included in the Fifth Amendment. The doctrine of double jeopardy is also recognized in many legal systems around the world, ensuring that once a person is acquitted or convicted, they are not subjected to repeated trials for the same alleged act.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is Double Jeopardy mentioned? → Article 20(2)
☛ What is the meaning of Double Jeopardy? → Not being punished more than once for the same crime
☛ Which Fundamental Right includes this principle? → Article 20 (Protection against Conviction)
☛ In the US, which amendment contains Double Jeopardy? → Fifth Amendment
☛ Who is protected by Double Jeopardy? → Any person who has been previously convicted or acquitted
question_hi: "किसी भी व्यक्ति को एक ही अपराध के लिए एक से अधिक दण्ड नहीं दिया जा सकता।" इस सिद्धांत को क्या कहते हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: दोहरे जोखिम
एकल दंड
आत्म-विमुखता
अनेक दंड
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दोहरे जोखिम

Explanation:
यह सिद्धांत कहता है कि किसी व्यक्ति को एक ही अपराध के लिए एक से अधिक बार दंडित नहीं किया जा सकता। इसे दोहरे जोखिम (Double Jeopardy) का सिद्धांत कहा जाता है। यह भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 20(2) में प्रदत्त मौलिक अधिकार है। इसके अनुसार, यदि किसी व्यक्ति को किसी अपराध के लिए पहले ही दोषी ठहराया जा चुका है या दंडित किया जा चुका है, तो उसे उसी अपराध के लिए पुनः अभियोजन का सामना नहीं करना पड़ेगा। यह सिद्धांत व्यक्ति को राज्य की मनमानी कार्रवाई से बचाता है और न्यायिक प्रक्रिया में निष्पक्षता सुनिश्चित करता है। संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के संविधान में भी यह सिद्धांत पांचवें संशोधन (Fifth Amendment) में शामिल है।

question: Which of the following is an autonomous institution related to rural areas? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Corporations
Municipality
Regional Councils
Panchayat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Panchayat

Explanation:
Panchayat is an autonomous institution related to rural areas in India, established under Part IX (Articles 243-243O) of the Constitution. It functions at three tiers: Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti at intermediate level, and Zila Parishad at district level. Other options like Corporations and Municipality are urban local bodies, while Regional Councils pertain to inter-state matters. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayats, empowering them to promote rural development and local self-governance. This system ensures democratic participation at the grassroots level.

question: According to Article 280 of Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is a ____. (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: Quasi-Federal Body
Quasi-Judicial body
Constitutional Body
Executive Body
solution:

question: The presence of _________ members is necessary for the meeting of the Lok Sabha in Parliament.  (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: 55 Members
60 members
45 Members
50 members
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 55 Members

Explanation:
According to the Indian Constitution, a quorum is required for the meeting of the Lok Sabha. Under Article 100(3), at least one-tenth of the total membership of the House must be present. The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 550, so one-tenth is 55 members. If the quorum is not met during a session, the Speaker or Chairperson may adjourn the meeting. This rule ensures the validity of parliamentary proceedings and democratic participation. The requirement of 55 members is crucial for maintaining the legitimacy of legislative decisions in the Lok Sabha.

question: When the Indian Constitution came into effect in 1949, how many Articles were there in it? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: 1000
200
395
947
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 395

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. At the time of its enforcement, the Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly over 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Over time, amendments have increased the number of Articles, but originally there were 395. Options 200 and 947 are incorrect; 1000 is also not correct. This is a common fact asked in competitive exams.

question: Which writ can be issued against both public and private individuals? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: Certiorari
Habeas corpus
Quo Warranto
Prohibition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Habeas corpus

Explanation:
Habeas corpus writ can be obtained by any person who has been illegally detained. This writ can be issued against both public and private individuals because its purpose is to protect the liberty of an individual from any unlawful detention. The writ is issued by a court to bring the detained person before the court to examine the legality of the detention. It is one of the fundamental rights and can be issued by the Supreme Court under Article 32 and by the High Courts under Article 226 of the Indian Constitution. Habeas corpus literally means 'to have the body' and serves as a powerful safeguard against arbitrary arrests.

question: Which of the following is not a constitutional body? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
National Commission for Women
National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Election Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Commission for Women

Explanation:
Under Part XVII of the Indian Constitution, Articles 338, 338A, and 338B grant constitutional status to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and National Commission for Backward Classes respectively. The Election Commission is constituted under Article 324, making it a constitutional body. The National Commission for Women was established in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, which is a statutory body, not a constitutional one. Therefore, among the four, only the National Commission for Women is not a constitutional body.

question: Which of the following article of Indian Constitution is related to the Assistant Powers of the Supreme Court? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: Article 243
Article 140
Article 143
Article 238
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 140

Explanation:
Article 140 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Ancillary Powers of the Supreme Court. This article empowers the Parliament to confer additional powers upon the Supreme Court by law to enable it to function more effectively. These powers include enforcing its judgments, summoning records, and passing necessary orders for securing the ends of justice. Article 140 helps the Supreme Court exercise its judicial review and ensure fair justice. In contrast, Article 243 relates to Panchayati Raj, Article 143 deals with the Advisory Jurisdiction of the President, and Article 238 (now repealed) dealt with special provisions for Jammu & Kashmir. Thus, the correct answer is Article 140.

question: Government of India Act 1919 was implemented due to which constitutional reform? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: Pitts India Act
Montague-Chelmsford Reform
Cripps Mission
Morley-Minto Reform
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Montague-Chelmsford Reform

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919 was implemented as a result of the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms. These reforms were based on the report of the then Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montague, and the Viceroy, Lord Chelmsford. The Act introduced dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces, dividing subjects into reserved and transferred categories. At the centre, a bicameral legislature was established, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly. For the first time, the Act recognized communal electorates, which fostered communalism. The Act came into effect in 1921 and remained in force until the 1935 Act.

question: In which article of the Indian Constitution there is a description of the provision related to 'the tenure of the governor'? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
Article 156 of the Indian Constitution deals with the tenure of the Governor. According to this article, the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, meaning there is no fixed term. The Governor may resign by writing to the President, and the President can remove the Governor at any time. However, in practice, the Governor's term is usually 5 years, but the President may terminate it earlier. This provision makes the Governor a representative of the President and plays a key role in center-state relations. question: When did the Right to Information Act (RTI) come into force? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)

2007
2012
2005
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2005

Explanation:
The Right to Information Act (RTI) is a landmark legislation in India that empowers citizens to access information from public authorities. It came into force on 12 October 2005, replacing the earlier Freedom of Information Act, 2002. The RTI Act promotes transparency and accountability in the functioning of government bodies. Under this act, any citizen can request information from a public authority, which must reply within 30 days. The act is a powerful tool against corruption and strengthens democracy. The RTI Act was passed by Parliament on 15 June 2005 and received presidential assent on 21 June 2005. It applies to all constitutional authorities, including the executive, legislature, and judiciary, except certain intelligence and security organizations.

question: The state's definition is given in which article of Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
Article 12 of the Indian Constitution provides the definition of the State. According to this definition, the State includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Governments and Legislatures of the States, as well as all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India. This definition ensures that fundamental rights are enforceable not only against the central and state governments but also against other public authorities.

question: The Chairman of 'Central Public Service Commission' can be removed by whom? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)

President
Speaker of Lok Sabha
Vice President
solution:

Explanation:
The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) can only be removed by the President of India. According to Article 317 of the Constitution, the President can remove the Chairman or any other member of UPSC after the Supreme Court, on a reference, has conducted an inquiry and found them guilty of misbehaviour or incapacity. This removal process requires a Supreme Court investigation, and the President acts based on its findings. This ensures the commission's independence and impartiality. The Prime Minister, Speaker of Lok Sabha, or Vice President do not have this authority, as the final power for removal of constitutional office bearers rests with the President.

question_hi: किसी भी राज्य में अनुसूचित जनजातियों एवं अनुसूचित जनजातियों के नियंत्रण एवं प्रशासन के संबंध में भारतीय संविधान में क्या प्रावधान दिए गए हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: पाँचवीं अनुसूची
छठी अनुसूची
आठवीं अनुसूची
पंद्रहवीं अनुसूची
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पाँचवीं अनुसूची

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की पाँचवीं अनुसूची किसी भी राज्य (असम, मेघालय, त्रिपुरा, मिजोरम को छोड़कर) में अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन और नियंत्रण से संबंधित प्रावधान करती है। इसके तहत अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों की घोषणा, उनके प्रशासन और जनजातीय सलाहकार परिषद के गठन का प्रावधान है। राष्ट्रपति को इन क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से संबंधित नियम बनाने का अधिकार है। छठी अनुसूची पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों के जनजातीय क्षेत्रों के लिए है, जबकि आठवीं अनुसूची भाषाओं से और पंद्रहवीं अनुसूची नगरपालिकाओं से संबंधित है।
